name: Ada Lovelace
summary: Backend engineer, four years shipping payment and ledger systems at two fintechs. Led the migration of a card-issuing platform off a monolith with no customer-facing downtime, and built the reconciliation service that closed a recurring six-figure gap.

bullets.text: Thesis on numerical methods for difference engines. Departmental prize for applied mathematics.

entries.title: Analytical Engine Ltd (card issuing for challenger banks)
entries.subtitle: Senior Backend Engineer

bullets.text: Led the migration of the card-issuing platform from a Rails monolith to Go services over nine months, cutting over without customer-facing downtime for 1.2M active cards.
Built the nightly reconciliation service matching issuer, scheme and ledger records, closing a recurring gap of roughly £180k a month within the first quarter.
Owned the on-call rotation for payments; drove p99 authorisation latency from 410ms to 140ms by moving hot-path lookups to a local cache.
Designed the double-entry ledger that replaced spreadsheet-based loan accounting, Postgres with event sourcing, auditable to the penny across 40k loans.
Wrote the underwriting rules engine in Python; reduced manual review of applications from 60% to 22% while holding default rates flat.
Built internal tooling for a data team in Python and SQL; automated a weekly report that had taken a day by hand.
Static checker for double-entry ledger schemas; catches unbalanced postings and orphaned accounts at CI time. Used by three fintechs in production.
Toy interpreter for a stack machine, written to understand how the first published algorithm would actually run.
Runs a quarterly meetup of 150 to 200 engineers; recruited speakers from six companies and moved it to a free venue.
Backend: Go, Python, Ruby, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS.
Domain: card issuing, ledgers, reconciliation, PCI DSS scope reduction.
